questions.stem: Before a fund switch, which information does the dealer give the client?

options.A: The charges, the dealer's incentives and the tax consequences of the switch
options.B: The past returns of both funds and the RR's own market outlook
options.C: The holdings list of the new fund and its next distribution date
options.D: The RR's commission grid and the dealer's annual financial statements

questions.rationale: Guidance on switch transactions says that the client learns the charges, the dealer's incentives and the tax consequences before the switch. Past returns or a market outlook can help, but they do not replace this disclosure.
questions.source_quote: "of charges associated with the transaction, dealers’ incentives for such a transaction" — research/sources/csa/cp-31-103-registration-requirements-companion-policy.txt 31-103CP 'Switch or change transactions', ~L3260

questions.stem: Fenella Marsh asks her RR to exchange her units of one mutual fund for units of a different fund. Which suitability points apply?

options.A: Only the purchase points, because her money stays invested
options.B: The points for both a sale and a purchase, such as tax on the sale and fit of the new fund
options.C: Only the sale points, because the new fund is at the same dealer
options.D: No points, because an exchange is not an investment action

questions.rationale: An exchange sells one security and buys another, so the points for selling and purchasing both apply. IDPC 3402(1) lists exchanges as an investment action. Looking only at the purchase ignores the tax and costs of the sale.
questions.source_quote: "Before a Dealer Member purchases, sells, withdraws, exchanges or transfers-out securities" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3402(1), ~L6793

questions.stem: Anneliese Grohmann sets up a pre-authorized plan that buys $500 of a balanced fund each month. When does the RR make a suitability determination for the plan?

options.A: Before each monthly purchase
options.B: Only at the next 36-month KYC review
options.C: When the plan is set up and when a triggering event occurs
options.D: Only if the fund's price falls by more than 10%

questions.rationale: Guidance says that pre-authorized purchases under an established plan do not need a determination before each purchase. The RR assesses the plan at set-up and when a trigger occurs. A check before every instalment is not required.
questions.source_quote: "Pre-authorized purchases or withdrawals pursuant to established plans do not require a suitability determination before each purchase or withdrawal." — research/sources/ciro/gn-3400-21-004-kyc-suitability-retail-clients.txt GN-3400-21-004 s.3.4.4, ~L634

questions.stem: Desmond Achebe asks to withdraw $50,000 from the bond part of his portfolio. After the withdrawal, his account will be mostly equities. What should the RR consider?

options.A: Nothing, because a withdrawal removes securities and needs no suitability review
options.B: Only whether the bonds have reached maturity
options.C: Only the tax that applies to the withdrawal
options.D: Whether the remaining, riskier portfolio still suits Desmond

questions.rationale: IDPC 3402(1) lists withdrawals as an investment action. The RR considers the effect on what remains. A withdrawal from the safe part of a portfolio leaves a riskier mix. So the claim that a withdrawal needs no review is wrong.
questions.source_quote: "Before a Dealer Member purchases, sells, withdraws, exchanges or transfers-out securities" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3402(1), ~L6793

questions.stem: Guidance links the concentration of a client's holdings to the work an RR does before a purchase. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The higher the concentration in one security, sector or industry, the more steps the RR takes and documents
options.B: Concentration matters only when the client is older than 65
options.C: Concentration is a dealer-level concern and not part of the RR's suitability work
options.D: A client who agrees to a concentrated position removes the need to document the steps

questions.rationale: Guidance says that the higher the concentration in a type of security, sector or industry, the more steps the RR takes and documents. Concentration is part of every determination, not only for older clients.
questions.source_quote: "Generally, the higher the concentration in a particular type of security, sector or industry, the more steps a Dealer or Registered Individual should take, and document" — research/sources/ciro/gn-3400-21-004-kyc-suitability-retail-clients.txt GN-3400-21-004 s.3.2.3, ~L493

questions.stem: Corisande Pell needs cash for a home purchase in 18 months. Her RR considers an exempt market fund with no redemption feature for her. Which factor weighs most against the purchase?

options.A: The fund's management fee is lower than the dealer average
options.B: Liquidity, because she may not be able to get cash from the fund when she needs it
options.C: Concentration, because the fund holds many properties
options.D: Tax, because exempt funds always pay capital gains

questions.rationale: IDPC 3402(1) requires the RR to consider the impact on the account, including liquidity. An illiquid exempt fund can stop her from getting cash for the home in 18 months. A diversified property fund does not raise the main concern here.
questions.source_quote: "the impact of the action on the retail client’s account, including the concentration of securities, derivatives or precious metals bullion, within the account and the liquidity" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3402(1)(i)(c), ~L6803

questions.stem: Wilfrid Okafor transfers in an account that holds a private real estate fund with no redemption feature. How does the suitability review apply to that fund?

options.A: The RR must sell the fund before the review of the rest of the account
options.B: The fund is outside suitability because another dealer sold it
options.C: The review of the fund may be limited, but the RR considers it in future recommendations
options.D: The client must sign a waiver before the dealer can hold the fund

questions.rationale: Guidance says that the review of an illiquid security with no redemption feature may be limited. The RR still considers it when making future recommendations. A security from another dealer is not outside suitability.
questions.source_quote: "However, the Registered Individual should consider this fact when making future recommendations for the client." — research/sources/ciro/gn-3400-21-004-kyc-suitability-retail-clients.txt GN-3400-21-004 s.3.4.4, ~L216

questions.stem: An RR plans to recommend a mutual fund purchase to a client. Which cost comparison does the suitability determination call for?

options.A: The costs of every mutual fund for sale in Canada
options.B: The costs of the funds that the RR personally owns
options.C: The costs of the funds with the highest past return only
options.D: The costs of a reasonable range of alternatives available at the dealer

questions.rationale: Under IDPC 3402(1), the RR considers a reasonable range of alternatives available through the dealer, including their costs. The rule does not require a comparison with every fund in Canada.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 1.19 Purchasing (costs and alternatives at the dealer; IDPC 3402(1))

questions.stem: Tomasz Wierzbicki opens an account and deposits shares from another dealer. The dealer cannot complete the suitability determination before it opens the account. What should the dealer do?

options.A: Complete the determination within a reasonable time and restrict investment actions until then
options.B: Refuse to open the account until the determination is complete
options.C: Allow normal trading and do the determination at the 36-month review
options.D: Ask Tomasz to sign a waiver of the suitability determination

questions.rationale: CIRO expects the dealer to complete the determination within a reasonable time after opening. Until then, it restricts investment actions, for example to liquidating trades, transfers or disbursements. Guidance does not require the dealer to refuse the account.
questions.source_quote: "complete the suitability determination within a reasonable time after opening the account" — research/sources/ciro/gn-3400-21-004-kyc-suitability-retail-clients.txt GN-3400-21-004 s.3.4.1, ~L581

questions.stem: When does the account appropriateness obligation apply?

options.A: At every periodic KYC review
options.B: Once, before the account is opened
options.C: Before each investment action in the account
options.D: Only when the client files a complaint

questions.rationale: Guidance calls account appropriateness a one-time obligation done before an account is opened. The suitability determination applies before each investment action, on triggers and on periodic review.
questions.source_quote: "Account appropriateness is a one-time obligation to be conducted before an account is opened." — research/sources/ciro/gn-3400-21-004-kyc-suitability-retail-clients.txt GN-3400-21-004 s.3.3.2, ~L535

questions.stem: Which comparison belongs to the account appropriateness obligation rather than the suitability determination?

options.A: A comparison of the costs of a reasonable range of securities at the dealer
options.B: A comparison of the resulting portfolio with the client's time horizon
options.C: A comparison of the account types available at the dealer
options.D: A comparison of the tax results of selling one position or another

questions.rationale: Account appropriateness asks which account, and which access, suits the person, so it compares account types. A suitability determination compares a reasonable range of investment actions and looks at the resulting portfolio.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 1.20 table (alternatives: account types vs reasonable range of actions)

questions.stem: Ottilie Brandt's advisory account was found appropriate when she opened it. She now asks her RR to buy a speculative junior mining stock. Which analysis is correct?

options.A: The purchase is suitable because the account passed the appropriateness check
options.B: The dealer must first repeat the account appropriateness check
options.C: No determination is needed because Ottilie asked for the stock
options.D: The RR must determine whether the purchase and her resulting portfolio are suitable

questions.rationale: This is an action question under IDPC 3402(1) and (4). An action can be unsuitable inside a suitable account, so the appropriate account does not settle it. The appropriateness check happens once, before opening.
questions.source_quote: "account portfolio of investments that would result from the investment action" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3402(4), ~L6844

questions.stem: After Xavier Lund opens a commission account, his dealer launches a new managed account programme. Which obligation does this raise?

options.A: The dealer determines whether his account and his scope of access remain suitable
options.B: The dealer must move Xavier into the new programme
options.C: The dealer must redo the one-time account appropriateness check
options.D: The launch has no effect on Xavier, because his account is already open

questions.rationale: Under IDPC 3402(3), the dealer continues to determine that the account and the scope of access remain suitable. This applies when the dealer offers new products or account types. The appropriateness check is not repeated.
questions.source_quote: "the scope of products, services and account relationships which the retail client has access to within the account are suitable for the retail client" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3402(3)(ii), ~L6842

questions.stem: Must a dealer reassess the client's account relationship at every periodic review?

options.A: Yes, at every periodic review and every suitability determination
options.B: No, it reassesses the relationship when a trigger warrants it
options.C: No, the relationship is never reassessed after the account opens
options.D: Yes, but only for accounts larger than $500,000

questions.rationale: Guidance says that dealers do not necessarily reassess the account relationship at each periodic review or suitability reassessment. They do so when a trigger warrants it. The obligation still continues after opening under IDPC 3402(3).
questions.source_quote: "We do not expect that Dealers will necessarily undertake a reassessment of the client’s account relationship at the time of each periodic review or suitability determination reassessment." — research/sources/ciro/gn-3400-21-004-kyc-suitability-retail-clients.txt GN-3400-21-004 s.3.4.4, ~L614

questions.stem: Rupert Vance, 84, has an order-execution-only account. For a year, he has had persistent trouble placing trades on the online platform. Which response fits the rules?

options.A: His RR gives him trade recommendations by phone within the account
options.B: The dealer changes nothing, because the account was appropriate at opening
options.C: The dealer determines whether the account remains suitable and discusses other account types
options.D: The dealer closes the account at once without telling Rupert

questions.rationale: Guidance treats persistent trouble with the online platform as a red flag. Under IDPC 3402(3)(i), the dealer determines whether the account remains suitable. Advice must not be given within an order-execution-only account.
questions.source_quote: "if it becomes obvious that a client is no longer capable of conducting online activities (e.g., persistent difficulties in accessing the Dealer’s online platform to place trades)" — research/sources/ciro/gn-3400-21-004-kyc-suitability-retail-clients.txt GN-3400-21-004 s.3.4.4, ~L200

questions.stem: A monthly supervisory review finds that an RR's own account often buys a stock just before his clients' orders in the same stock. Which IDPC 3945(2) detection area does this involve?

options.A: Undue concentration of securities
options.B: Deterioration in the quality of client holdings
options.C: Inappropriate or high-risk trading strategies
options.D: Conflicts between RR trading and client trading activity

questions.rationale: IDPC 3945(2) requires retail supervision policies to detect conflicts between RR trading and client trading activity. The RR's trades come before his clients' trades in the same stock. No concentration or quality problem is described.
questions.source_quote: "conflict of interest between Registered Representative, Investment Representative, Portfolio Manager and Associate Portfolio Manager and client trading activity" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3945(2)(v), ~L10011

questions.stem: Dorotea Lindahl's KYC was reviewed last month. Now bond holdings from her late husband's estate are transferred into her account. Must the dealer review suitability?

options.A: Yes, because a transfer-in of securities is a trigger
options.B: No, because her KYC is less than one month old
options.C: No, because estate transfers are outside the suitability rules
options.D: Only if Dorotea asks for a review in writing

questions.rationale: IDPC 3402(2)(i) makes the receipt of securities by deposit or transfer a trigger. The recent KYC review does not remove it. The dealer reviews the account within a reasonable time.
questions.source_quote: "are received or delivered into the client’s account by way of deposit or transfer" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3402(2)(i), ~L6815

questions.stem: The stock market falls 18% in one month. Which statement about the dealer's suitability obligations is correct?

options.A: The fall is a mandatory trigger to review every account at once
options.B: The fall is not a mandatory trigger, but the RDI says whether the dealer reviews in this case
options.C: The fall requires the dealer to sell all equity funds in client accounts
options.D: The fall ends the dealer's suitability obligations until markets recover

questions.rationale: Significant market fluctuations are not a listed trigger in IDPC 3402(2). The relationship disclosure must state whether the dealer reviews suitability in the event of significant market fluctuations.
questions.source_quote: "in the event of significant market fluctuations" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3216(5)(ii)(d)(IV), ~L5906

questions.stem: Gideon Marsh tells his RR that he lost his job and may need cash soon. What should the dealer consider until it re-evaluates his KYC information?

options.A: Allowing new speculative purchases to make up his lost income
options.B: Closing his account and sending him a cheque
options.C: Restricting the account to liquidating trades, transfers or disbursements
options.D: Waiting for his next 36-month review before it takes any step

questions.rationale: Guidance says that after a significant KYC change, such as a job loss, the dealer should consider a restriction. It allows only liquidating trades, transfers or disbursements until the KYC is re-evaluated.
questions.source_quote: "the Dealer should consider restricting activities in the client’s account to liquidating trades, transfers or disbursements, until such time as the Dealer has had a chance to re-evaluate the client’s KYC information" — research/sources/ciro/gn-3400-21-004-kyc-suitability-retail-clients.txt GN-3400-21-004 s.2.11.2, ~L425

questions.stem: After a trigger, what determines how extensive the suitability review must be?

options.A: Only the market value of the account
options.B: Only the number of years the client has been with the dealer
options.C: Only the client's age and the level of the stock market
options.D: The type of event, the client relationship, the dealer's services and the securities held

questions.rationale: Guidance says that the extent of the review depends on the type of event and the client relationship. It also depends on the dealer's services and the securities in the account. Account size alone does not decide it.
questions.source_quote: "the type of event that triggered the obligation to reassess suitability, the relationship between the client and the Dealer or Registered Individual, the services and securities offered by the Dealer, and the types of the securities within the account" — research/sources/ciro/gn-3400-21-004-kyc-suitability-retail-clients.txt GN-3400-21-004 s.3.4.4, ~L627

questions.stem: Under IDPC 3945(2), which item must a dealer's retail supervision policies specifically address the detection of?

options.A: Excessive transfers and trade cancellations that indicate possible unauthorized trading
options.B: Changes in a client's preferred method of statement delivery
options.C: The number of new accounts that each RR opens each month
options.D: Client comments about the speed of the dealer's website

questions.rationale: IDPC 3945(2) lists excessive transfers and trade cancellations that indicate possible unauthorized trading. It also lists unsuitable and excessive trading. Statement delivery, account openings and website comments are not on the list.
questions.source_quote: "excessive transaction transfers and trade cancellations indicating possible unauthorized trading" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3945(2)(vi), ~L10013

questions.stem: RR Philippa Grange takes over an account from an RR who left the dealer. Under IDPC 3215(2), who must acknowledge in writing that the account application was reviewed?

options.A: The client and the dealer's Chief Compliance Officer
options.B: Philippa and the designated Supervisor
options.C: The departing RR and the client
options.D: Philippa and the client's trusted contact person

questions.rationale: Under IDPC 3215(2)(ii), the new RR and the designated Supervisor acknowledge in writing that they reviewed the account application. They also update it if necessary.
questions.source_quote: "the designated Supervisor acknowledge, in writing, that the account application was reviewed and, if necessary, updated" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3215(2)(ii), ~L5785

questions.stem: Henrietta Szabo transfers $200,000 of stocks into her existing advisory account. Which holdings must the resulting suitability review cover?

options.A: Only the stocks that she transferred in
options.B: Only the holdings bought in the past 12 months
options.C: The account and all the securities in it, against the IDPC 3402(1) criteria
options.D: Only holdings that the RR recommended himself

questions.rationale: After a trigger, IDPC 3402(2) requires a review of the client's account and the securities in it. The test is whether the IDPC 3402(1) criteria are met. A review of only the new stocks misses the effect on the whole portfolio.
questions.source_quote: "review the retail client’s account and the securities, derivatives or precious metals bullion, in the retail client’s account to determine whether the criteria in subsection 3402(1) are met" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3402(2), ~L6812

questions.stem: Rosalind Achterberg's divorce is final, and her net worth falls by half. Why does this matter to the suitability of her account?

options.A: It matters only if her mailing address also changes
options.B: It does not matter, because personal events are not KYC information
options.C: It matters only at her next periodic KYC review
options.D: It can change her financial circumstances and risk capacity, so it is a KYC trigger

questions.rationale: A divorce is a material change in circumstances that can shift capacity and objectives. A change in KYC information that could make the account unsuitable is a trigger under IDPC 3402(2)(iii). The dealer updates the KYC within a reasonable time.
questions.source_quote: "the Dealer Member becomes aware of a change in the retail client" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3402(2)(iii), ~L6819

questions.stem: Research shows that a new regulation will hurt the oil sector. Several of an RR's clients hold 40% of their accounts in oil stocks. What is the main suitability concern?

options.A: Concentration risk, because a sector-specific change may need a reassessment
options.B: Currency risk, because oil is priced in US dollars
options.C: No concern, because market research is never relevant to suitability
options.D: Liquidity risk, because oil stocks cannot be sold on an exchange

questions.rationale: A shock to one sector can create concentration risk for clients who hold a lot of it. A sector-specific change may need a reassessment. Market research is part of the ongoing suitability picture.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 1.22 Product and market research (sector shock creates concentration risk)

questions.stem: The general market declines. At the dealer level, must the dealer reassess each security that it has approved for its product shelf?

options.A: Yes, every approved security must be reassessed at once
options.B: Usually not, because a general market change usually does not require a reassessment of individual securities
options.C: Yes, but only the securities with the highest fees
options.D: No, approved securities are never reassessed after approval

questions.rationale: Product due diligence guidance says that a general market change usually does not require a reassessment of individual approved securities. A change in a specific security can still require one.
questions.source_quote: "we generally would not consider it a change requiring reassessment of individual securities" — research/sources/ciro/gn-3300-21-001-product-due-diligence-kyp.txt GN-3300-21-001 Monitor and review, ~L185

questions.stem: A real estate fund held by Florian Dubois suspends redemptions. How should his RR classify this change?

options.A: A change in the client, so it is a KYC trigger
options.B: A change in the environment, so it is never a trigger
options.C: A change in a security, so it is a trigger to review the account
options.D: A change of RR, so the new RR must verify the KYC

questions.rationale: Suspended redemptions are a change in the product. A change in a security that could make it unsuitable is a trigger under IDPC 3402(2)(iv). It also links to the dealer's product due diligence monitoring.
questions.source_quote: "the Dealer Member becomes aware of a change in a security, derivative or precious metals bullion" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3402(2)(iv), ~L6822

questions.stem: Which statement about long-run trends, such as demographics, technology and inflation, is correct?

options.A: They are a listed trigger that requires an immediate review of every account
options.B: They are not relevant to suitability because they are not about one client
options.C: They require the dealer to remove products from its shelf
options.D: They shift long-run assumptions, and the RR usually addresses them at the periodic review

questions.rationale: Emerging issues and trends shift long-run assumptions and preferences, such as ESG preferences. The RR usually addresses them at the periodic review. They are not a listed trigger in IDPC 3402(2).
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 1.22 Emerging issues, financial trends, economic trends and world news

questions.stem: An RR analyzes a change that may affect a client's suitability determination. What is the first question to ask?

options.A: What changed: the client, the product or the environment?
options.B: How much commission will the change produce?
options.C: Has the client complained about the change?
options.D: Which other dealers have seen the same change?

questions.rationale: The analysis starts with what changed: the client, the product or the environment. Next, the RR finds which KYC factor or holding it affects. Last, the RR checks whether the resulting portfolio still meets IDPC 3402(1).
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 1.22 Analyze in three steps

questions.stem: Marisol Quintero, 61, learns that she has a serious illness. She will need $60,000 for care within a year. Which part of her profile does this change most directly?

options.A: Her investment knowledge
options.B: Her liquidity needs and time horizon
options.C: Her tax residency
options.D: Her choice of trusted contact person

questions.rationale: An illness can shift liquidity needs and time horizon. Marisol now needs $60,000 within a year. This KYC change could make her account unsuitable, so it is a trigger. Her investment knowledge does not change.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 1.22 Material change to the client's circumstances (illness shifts liquidity and horizon)

questions.stem: RR Casimir Wolanski wants to give hockey tickets to the treasurer of a corporate client, to thank her for the company's business. When is this allowed?

options.A: When the tickets cost less than $500
options.B: When Casimir discloses the gift to his branch manager afterwards
options.C: When the corporate client gives prior written consent
options.D: When the treasurer agrees to accept the tickets

questions.rationale: IDPC 3116 prohibits a gratuity or benefit to a client's employee in relation to the client's business. The prohibition does not apply if the client gives prior written consent. The treasurer's own agreement is not the client's consent.
questions.source_quote: "does not apply if the prior written consent of the client has been obtained" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3116(2), ~L5074

questions.stem: A fund company offers a free trip to the RRs who sell the most units of its mutual fund this year. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The trip is allowed if each RR discloses it to clients
options.B: The trip is allowed because it is not cash
options.C: The trip is allowed if the dealer approves it in writing
options.D: The trip is a prohibited non-cash mutual fund sales incentive

questions.rationale: IDPC 3117 prohibits accepting or paying non-cash sales incentives for the sale of mutual fund products. A trip tied to sales of one fund is such an incentive. Disclosure does not make it allowed.
questions.source_quote: "must not, directly or indirectly, accept or pay any non-cash sales incentive in connection with the sale or distribution of mutual fund products" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3117(2), ~L5080

questions.stem: A dealer runs a contest in which RRs earn a trip. Eligibility depends on revenue from all the products and services that the dealer offers. Is this a prohibited non-cash mutual fund sales incentive?

options.A: No, because eligibility for the internal programme covers all of the dealer's products and services
options.B: Yes, because any non-cash prize to an RR is prohibited
options.C: Yes, because some of the revenue comes from mutual funds
options.D: No, but only if the trip costs less than one month of the RR's pay

questions.rationale: IDPC 3117(3) excludes non-cash incentives from a dealer's internal programme when eligibility is set on all its services and products. This contest meets that condition, so mutual fund revenue in the total does not make it prohibited.
questions.source_quote: "non-cash sales incentives earned or awarded through a Dealer Member’s internal incentive program for which eligibility is determined with respect to all services and products offered by the Dealer Member" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3117(3)(i), ~L5092

questions.stem: A dealer tells Ignacio Ferro that he gets a margin loan only if he also buys the dealer's proprietary balanced fund. Which statement is correct?

options.A: This is allowed relationship pricing
options.B: This is prohibited tied selling
options.C: This is allowed if the fund is suitable for Ignacio
options.D: This is allowed if the dealer discloses the condition in writing

questions.rationale: IDPC 3118 prohibits making the purchase of a product a condition of supplying another product. Relationship pricing gives a benefit, but it does not impose a condition. Disclosure or suitability does not cure tied selling.
questions.source_quote: "as a condition, or on terms that would appear to a reasonable person to be a condition, of supplying, continuing to supply or selling a product" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3118(1), ~L5106

questions.stem: A dealer offers a lower annual fee to clients who keep more assets in their accounts with it. No purchase is a condition of any service. Which statement is correct?

options.A: This is prohibited tied selling
options.B: This is a prohibited non-cash sales incentive
options.C: This is permitted relationship pricing
options.D: This is allowed only with each client's written consent

questions.rationale: IDPC 3118(2) lets a dealer offer relationship pricing or other beneficial selling arrangements. Here no purchase is a condition of a service. So it is not tied selling under IDPC 3118(1).
questions.source_quote: "relationship pricing or other beneficial selling arrangements" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3118(2), ~L5109

questions.stem: A dealer must disclose a material conflict of interest to a client. What must the disclosure describe?

options.A: Only the name of the RR involved in the conflict
options.B: Only the dollar amount that the dealer earns from the conflict
options.C: Only the date on which the dealer found the conflict
options.D: The nature and extent of the conflict, its potential impact and risk, and how it is addressed

questions.rationale: IDPC 3113(2) requires disclosure of the nature and extent of the conflict and its potential impact on and risk to the client. It also states how the conflict is addressed.
questions.source_quote: "how the conflict of interest has been, or will be, addressed" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3113(2)(i)(c), ~L4974

questions.stem: Two years after Hesper Lowell opens her account, her dealer identifies a new material conflict that a reasonable client would expect to know. When must the dealer disclose it?

options.A: In a timely manner, when it identifies the conflict
options.B: At her next periodic KYC review
options.C: Only if she asks about conflicts
options.D: Only when she next opens a new account

questions.rationale: IDPC 3113 requires disclosure before the account opens, or in a timely manner when a conflict that must be disclosed is identified. Waiting for the next periodic review is not timely.
questions.source_quote: "in a timely manner, upon identification of a conflict that must be disclosed" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3113(2)(iii)(b), ~L4980

questions.stem: RR Benedetta Rossi's spouse earns a bonus each time clients buy shares of one private issuer. Her dealer finds no control that addresses this in the clients' best interest. What must Benedetta do?

options.A: Recommend the shares after she gives each client written disclosure
options.B: Avoid the conflict and not recommend the shares
options.C: Recommend the shares only to clients with a high risk tolerance
options.D: Recommend the shares if each client signs a waiver

questions.rationale: IDPC 3111(2) requires an Approved Person to avoid a material conflict that cannot be addressed in the client's best interest. Disclosure alone never satisfies the rule under IDPC 3113(3), so disclosure or a waiver does not help.
questions.source_quote: "must avoid any material conflict of interest between the client and the Approved Person if the conflict is not, or cannot be, otherwise addressed in the best interest of the client" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3111(2), ~L4950

questions.stem: A dealer receives extra payments from a fund company for making its funds available for sale. How do CSA and CIRO staff view this?

options.A: As a minor conflict that needs no action
options.B: As a conflict that disclosure alone resolves
options.C: As a conflict that almost always is material
options.D: As a conflict only if the funds lose money

questions.rationale: CSA and CIRO staff say that material conflicts almost always arise when a firm receives third-party compensation for making a product available. The dealer must address the conflict in the client's best interest, and disclosure alone is not enough.
questions.source_quote: "material conflicts of interest almost always arise when a firm receives additional third-party compensation when making a product available for sale" — research/sources/ciro/csa-ciro-staff-notice-31-363-conflicts-of-interest-page.txt CSA/CIRO SN 31-363, ~L180

questions.stem: RR Lorcan Doyle is also the branch manager. He wants to become a director of a local credit union. Who may approve his outside activity request?

options.A: Lorcan himself, because he is the branch manager
options.B: Any client of the branch who knows him
options.C: CIRO, through its acknowledgement of his NRD notice
options.D: Someone at the dealer other than Lorcan

questions.rationale: Guidance says that Approved Persons should never adjudicate their own outside activity request. The dealer's approval process must be impartial. A CIRO acknowledgement on NRD is not an approval of the activity.
questions.source_quote: "Approved Persons should never adjudicate their own outside activity request." — research/sources/ciro/gn-2500-22-001-outside-activities.txt GN-2500-22-001 s.3.5, ~L116

questions.stem: RR Yvaine Castell changes the scope of an approved outside activity. Within what time must the change be reported through NRD?

options.A: Within 30 days of the change
options.B: Within 10 days of the change
options.C: Within 90 days of the change
options.D: At the next annual outside activity canvass

questions.rationale: Changes to outside activities must be reported within 30 days of the change under section 4.1 of NI 33-109. The dealer's annual canvass does not replace this deadline.
questions.source_quote: "must be reported within 30 days of the change, pursuant to section 4.1 of NI 33-109" — research/sources/ciro/gn-2500-22-001-outside-activities.txt GN-2500-22-001 s.5, ~L149

questions.stem: RR Saoirse Kenna files an NRD notice for a new outside activity and receives CIRO's acknowledgement. She starts the activity the next day. Which statement is correct?

options.A: She acted correctly, because CIRO acknowledged the notice
options.B: The acknowledgement is not an approval, and she needs the dealer's prior approval
options.C: She acted correctly, because outside activities need only disclosure
options.D: She needs approval only if the activity is paid

questions.rationale: Guidance says that CIRO's acknowledgement of an NRD notice is not an approval of the activity. Under IDPC 2554(2), she must inform the dealer and get its prior approval. Approval applies whether or not the activity is paid.
questions.source_quote: "acknowledgement of these notices, via NRD, does not represent our approval of the individual’s outside activity" — research/sources/ciro/gn-2500-22-001-outside-activities.txt GN-2500-22-001 s.5, ~L157

questions.stem: RR Thorvald Engstrom has approval to run a small tax-preparation business. He wants to meet its customers in the dealer's office and use his dealer email for it. What should the dealer do?

options.A: Allow it, because the activity is already approved
options.B: Allow it if Thorvald pays rent for the office
options.C: Refuse the use of its premises and email for the activity
options.D: Allow it only for customers who are also dealer clients

questions.rationale: Guidance says that dealers should not permit the use of their premises, logos, staff or office facilities, such as email, for outside activities. Approval of the activity does not extend to dealer resources.
questions.source_quote: "Dealers should not permit the use of its premises, records, logos, trade name(s), stationery, support staff, office facilities (e.g., mail, fax, email, etc.) for the purposes of outside activities." — research/sources/ciro/gn-2500-22-001-outside-activities.txt GN-2500-22-001 s.3.4, ~L103

questions.stem: A listed company invites RR Marguerite Pellerin to join its board. Many of her clients hold its shares. What is the main concern for the dealer's approval decision?

options.A: The board fees are too low to matter
options.B: The role is unpaid volunteer work
options.C: The company is listed on a Canadian exchange
options.D: The role may prevent her from giving fully informed and unbiased advice

questions.rationale: Guidance names positions with public issuers as activities that may prevent fully informed and unbiased counsel. Her clients hold the company's shares, so the conflict is direct. Pay level does not remove the concern.
questions.source_quote: "Outside activities (e.g. positions with public issuers) that may prevent an Approved Person from providing fully informed and unbiased counsel" — research/sources/ciro/gn-2500-22-001-outside-activities.txt GN-2500-22-001 s.3.2, ~L93

questions.stem: RR Anselm Kovac leads a religious congregation. A member is susceptible to his influence. Anselm knows the member's adult son, who asks Anselm to open an account. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Anselm must not buy, sell or recommend securities for the son
options.B: Anselm may serve the son because the son is not a congregation member
options.C: Anselm may serve the son if the son signs a waiver
options.D: Anselm may serve the son after he discloses his role to the dealer

questions.rationale: A registered individual in a position of influence must not trade for or advise a person they know is the child of a susceptible individual. A religious leader is a listed position of influence. Disclosure does not lift this prohibition.
questions.source_quote: "an Approved Person knows is a spouse, parent, sibling, grandparent or child of the foregoing individual" — research/sources/ciro/gn-2500-22-001-outside-activities.txt GN-2500-22-001 s.5, ~L173

questions.stem: RR Ewan MacRury's approved outside activity sometimes keeps him away from the office during market hours. Which supervisory step fits the dealer's duty?

options.A: Telling his clients to wait until he returns
options.B: Having an alternate representative available for his clients
options.C: Letting him take client orders by personal text message
options.D: Withdrawing his approval for the activity without review

questions.rationale: Guidance on outside activities lists an alternate representative for clients, where necessary, as a monitoring step. IDPC 2554(2) also requires dealer policies to address continuous service to clients.
questions.source_quote: "where necessary, having an alternate representative available for the client" — research/sources/ciro/gn-2500-22-001-outside-activities.txt GN-2500-22-001 s.4 (citing 31-103CP s.13.4), ~L143

questions.stem: RR Dagny Holt starts a paid consulting business. She tells her dealer about it three months later. What should the dealer do?

options.A: Nothing, because she did report the activity
options.B: Approve it with retroactive effect and take no other step
options.C: Take appropriate supervisory action for the late report
options.D: Report her only if a client complains about the business

questions.rationale: Guidance expects dealers to take supervisory action when they find non-compliance, such as no report or a late report of an outside activity. IDPC 2554 requires prior approval, which Dagny did not get.
questions.source_quote: "taking appropriate supervisory actions when the Dealer identifies non-compliance with its policies on outside activities, such as no or late reporting of an outside activity" — research/sources/ciro/gn-2500-22-001-outside-activities.txt GN-2500-22-001 s.4 (citing 31-103CP s.13.4), ~L142

questions.stem: Once a year, a client gives RR Ilario Benedetti a small box of chocolates at the holidays. Which statement is correct?

options.A: He must refuse it, because all gifts from clients are prohibited
options.B: He may accept it only after the dealer approves it in writing
options.C: He must pay the client for the value of the gift
options.D: He may accept it because it is non-monetary, of minimal value and infrequent

questions.rationale: IDPC 3115 allows consideration that is non-monetary, of minimal value and infrequent. A reasonable person would not question whether it created a conflict. A yearly box of chocolates meets these conditions.
questions.source_quote: "infrequent such that it will not cause a reasonable person to question whether it created a conflict of interest or otherwise improperly influenced the Dealer Member" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3115(2)(i)(a)(I), ~L5007

questions.stem: After a strong year, a client offers RR Perpetua Lang a $2,000 cash bonus as thanks. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Accepting it is a prohibited personal financial dealing
options.B: She may accept it if she reports it on her tax return
options.C: She may accept it because the client offered it freely
options.D: She may accept it if she discloses it to the client in writing

questions.rationale: IDPC 3115 prohibits accepting any consideration from anyone other than the dealer for activities on behalf of a client. Cash is monetary, so the minimal-value exception does not apply.
questions.source_quote: "accepting any consideration, including remuneration, gratuity or benefit, from any person other than the Dealer Member for any activities conducted on behalf of a client" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3115(2)(i)(a), ~L5004

questions.stem: RR Cormac Byrne has dealer approval to work as a tax preparer outside the dealer. A client pays him a normal fee to prepare her tax return. Which statement is correct?

options.A: It is prohibited, because all payments from clients are prohibited
options.B: It is not prohibited consideration, because it is pay for an approved outside activity
options.C: It is allowed only if the fee is less than $100
options.D: It is allowed only if the client is a Related Person

questions.rationale: IDPC 3115 says that compensation from a client for services through an approved outside activity is not prohibited consideration. Without the dealer's approval of the activity, the payment would be prohibited.
questions.source_quote: "Compensation received from a client in exchange for services provided through an approved outside activity" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3115(2)(i)(a)(II), ~L5012

questions.stem: RR Elspeth Rowan gets a home mortgage on normal terms from a chartered bank. The bank is also a client of her dealer. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The mortgage is prohibited, because the bank is a client
options.B: The mortgage is allowed only if the bank is a Related Person
options.C: The mortgage is allowed, because the bank lends to the public in its normal course
options.D: The mortgage is allowed only if a client consents in writing

questions.rationale: IDPC 3115 permits borrowing from a client that is a financial institution whose business includes lending to the public, in the normal course. The Related Person exception is a separate route and is not needed here.
questions.source_quote: "the client is a financial institution whose business includes lending money to the public and the borrowing is in the normal course of the institution’s business" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3115(2)(iii)(a)(I), ~L5023

questions.stem: A client who is not related to RR Barnaby Quist faces a short-term cash need. Barnaby wants to lend her $5,000 from his own savings. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The loan is allowed if the dealer approves it in writing first
options.B: The loan is allowed if the client signs a promissory note
options.C: The loan is allowed because it helps the client
options.D: The loan is prohibited, because the client is not a Related Person

questions.rationale: IDPC 3115 prohibits lending to a client. The only exception is a Related Person, with dealer policies followed and prior written dealer approval. The client is unrelated, so dealer approval alone cannot permit the loan.
questions.source_quote: "Lending money, or providing a guarantee in relation to a loan of money, securities or any other assets to a client, unless" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3115(2)(iv)(a), ~L5045

questions.stem: An elderly client with no family asks RR Guinevere Tolland to act as her power of attorney. Guinevere is not related to her. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Guinevere must not accept, because the client is not a Related Person
options.B: Guinevere may accept if the client's lawyer prepares the document
options.C: Guinevere may accept if she discloses the role to the client's bank
options.D: Guinevere may accept if the client has no other trusted person

questions.rationale: IDPC 3115 prohibits acting as a power of attorney or having control over a client's finances. The exceptions are a Related Person or authority under a discretionary or managed account. Neither applies here.
questions.source_quote: "Acting as a Power of Attorney, trustee, executor, or otherwise having full or partial control or authority over the financial affairs of a client, unless" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3115(2)(v)(a), ~L5055

questions.stem: Which control or authority over an unrelated client's finances does IDPC 3115 permit for an RR?

options.A: Acting as trustee of the client's family trust
options.B: Authority used solely under the terms of a discretionary account agreement
options.C: Acting as the executor of the client's estate
options.D: Holding a power of attorney over the client's bank accounts

questions.rationale: IDPC 3115 prohibits control or authority over a client's finances. The prohibition does not apply to authority used solely under the terms of a discretionary or managed account. Trustee, executor and power of attorney roles stay prohibited.
questions.source_quote: "does not apply to the extent that the control or authority is solely exercised consistent with the terms of the discretionary account" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3115(2)(v)(b), ~L5065

questions.stem: RR Lysander Moore proposes an investment club. He and several clients would pool their money, and he would make the investment decisions. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The club is allowed if each client signs a club agreement
options.B: The club is allowed if Lysander invests the most money
options.C: The club mixes his money with clients' money, and guidance says it should be prohibited
options.D: The club is allowed if it holds only listed securities

questions.rationale: Staff guidance says that investment clubs, where the representative and clients invest together and the representative decides, should be prohibited. IDPC 3115's list is not exhaustive, so this comingling falls under the general prohibition.
questions.source_quote: "investment clubs, where the Approved Person and clients invest together, with the Approved Person making decisions on behalf of the investment club" — research/sources/ciro/mfda-msn-0047-personal-financial-dealings-with-clients.txt MFDA MSN-0047 (c), ~L42

questions.stem: How often do CSA and CIRO staff expect a dealer to review its conflict-of-interest policies and procedures?

options.A: Only when CIRO starts an examination
options.B: Every five years
options.C: Only after a client complaint
options.D: At least annually, and more often if the business model or products change

questions.rationale: Staff expect a periodic review at least annually. A review is needed more often if the firm's business structure, model or product offering changes. Waiting for an examination or a complaint is not enough.
questions.source_quote: "the process for periodic review (to be conducted at least annually" — research/sources/ciro/csa-ciro-staff-notice-31-363-conflicts-of-interest-page.txt CSA/CIRO SN 31-363, policies and procedures, ~L472

questions.stem: CSA and CIRO staff reviewed dealers' conflicts training. Which flaw did they find made training inadequate?

options.A: It was too generic and not tailored to the firm's business
options.B: It used examples of the firm's own conflicts
options.C: It explained how to escalate a conflict
options.D: It included compliance staff

questions.rationale: Staff found training inadequate if it was too generic for the firm's business. It also failed if it gave no examples of the firm's own conflicts or did not explain how to report or escalate.
questions.source_quote: "it was too generic and not specific or tailored to the firm’s business operations or size" — research/sources/ciro/csa-ciro-staff-notice-31-363-conflicts-of-interest-page.txt CSA/CIRO SN 31-363, training, ~L482

questions.stem: A dealer plans its conflict-of-interest training. Whom do CSA and CIRO staff expect the training to include?

options.A: Only RRs who sell proprietary products
options.B: All registered individuals and supervisory staff, including compliance staff
options.C: Only new employees in their first year
options.D: Only branch managers and senior executives

questions.rationale: Staff expect conflicts training for all registered individuals and supervisory staff, and they expect this to include compliance staff. Training that leaves out people who should attend is inadequate.
questions.source_quote: "We expect that this would include compliance staff." — research/sources/ciro/csa-ciro-staff-notice-31-363-conflicts-of-interest-page.txt CSA/CIRO SN 31-363, training, ~L487

questions.stem: A dealer keeps a conflicts inventory. Which item do CSA and CIRO staff expect it to record for each material conflict?

options.A: The personal holdings of each client affected
options.B: The market share of each competing dealer
options.C: Who identified the conflict and assessed whether it is material
options.D: The home address of each RR involved

questions.rationale: Staff expect the inventory to record who at the firm identified the conflict and assessed its materiality. It also records the description, materiality criteria, impact and risk, controls and client disclosure.
questions.source_quote: "who at the firm was involved in identifying the conflict and making the assessment of whether it is material" — research/sources/ciro/csa-ciro-staff-notice-31-363-conflicts-of-interest-page.txt CSA/CIRO SN 31-363, record keeping, ~L511

questions.stem: A dealer keeps records of its material conflicts. How should the level of detail relate to each conflict?

options.A: All conflicts need the same short entry
options.B: Only conflicts that caused client losses need records
options.C: Records are needed only for conflicts disclosed to clients
options.D: As a conflict becomes more material, the records need more detail

questions.rationale: Staff say that as the materiality of a conflict increases, the records need greater detail to demonstrate compliance. IDPC 3804(2) requires records that demonstrate compliance with conflicts requirements.
questions.source_quote: "As the materiality of a conflict increases, there should be greater detail in the records maintained to demonstrate compliance." — research/sources/ciro/csa-ciro-staff-notice-31-363-conflicts-of-interest-page.txt CSA/CIRO SN 31-363, record keeping, ~L503

questions.stem: Why do CSA and CIRO staff expect the dealer, rather than each RR, to lead on conflicts from the product shelf and pay structure?

options.A: An individual RR cannot change the product shelf or the pay structure
options.B: RRs have no duty to identify conflicts
options.C: Conflicts from pay structures are never material
options.D: Only the dealer may disclose conflicts to clients

questions.rationale: Staff expect firms to take the lead on material conflicts, including the product shelf and compensation structures. An individual RR cannot change those. RRs still must identify and report conflicts under IDPC 3110.
questions.source_quote: "We expect firms to take the lead in addressing material conflicts of interest, including those related to the firm’s product shelf and compensation structures." — research/sources/ciro/csa-ciro-staff-notice-31-363-conflicts-of-interest-page.txt CSA/CIRO SN 31-363 intro, ~L22

questions.stem: RR Fintan Hale tells a client that a small-cap stock is guaranteed to return 12% this year. The stock later rises 15%. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Fintan did nothing wrong, because the client made money
options.B: The promise of a return can breach the standards of conduct, whatever the result
options.C: Fintan did nothing wrong, because the promise was oral
options.D: A breach occurs only if the client complains

questions.rationale: A promise of returns is conduct likely to diminish investor confidence under IDPC 1402(2). The breach is in the promise, not the result. A complaint is not needed for a breach.
questions.source_quote: "is likely to diminish investor confidence in the integrity of securities or derivatives markets" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 1402(2)(iv), ~L1200

questions.stem: RR Odalys Ferreira arranges for several clients to buy shares of a private company. The trades are not processed through her dealer's books. Which statement is correct?

options.A: This is allowed if the clients sign a release
options.B: This is allowed because the shares are not listed
options.C: This breaches the standards of conduct toward her dealer
options.D: This is allowed if she earns no commission

questions.rationale: Trades off the dealer's books are a breach of the standards of conduct between an RR and her firm. They also breach dealer policy, which IDPC 1402(2) treats as possible misconduct. A release or lack of commission does not cure this.
questions.source_quote: "fails to comply with a legal, regulatory, contractual or other obligation, including the rules, requirements, and policies of a Regulated Person" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 1402(2)(ii), ~L1196

questions.stem: Under IDPC 1403, which statement about a dealer's responsibility for its people is correct?

options.A: A dealer is responsible only for acts that its Directors approve
options.B: A dealer is responsible only for acts during office hours
options.C: A dealer is responsible only for intentional misconduct
options.D: A dealer is responsible for all acts and omissions of its employees, partners, Directors and officers

questions.rationale: IDPC 1403 makes dealers responsible for all acts and omissions of their employees, partners, Directors and officers. Approved Persons must also avoid acts that would cause the dealer to breach CIRO requirements.
questions.source_quote: "Dealer Members are responsible for all acts and omissions of their employees, partners, Directors and officers" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 1403(1)(i), ~L1204

questions.stem: RR Hamish Lockhart wants to sell a growth fund to a new client. He tells her to choose "high" on the risk questionnaire so that the fund will fit. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Pressing the client on her questionnaire answers breaches the standards of conduct
options.B: This is allowed if the client agrees to the change
options.C: This is allowed because the client signs the questionnaire
options.D: This is a breach only if the fund later loses money

questions.rationale: Pressure on a client's risk-questionnaire answers breaches the standards of conduct. It also creates false KYC records for the dealer. The client's signature or agreement does not cure the pressure.
questions.source_quote: "displays an unreasonable departure from standards that are expected to be observed by a Regulated Person" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 1402(2)(iii), ~L1198

questions.stem: RR Leopold Asante sells a falling stock in an advisory client's account while she is on vacation. He wants to protect her from losses. She did not authorize the sale. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The sale is allowed because it protected the client
options.B: The sale is an unauthorized trade, and good intent is not a defence
options.C: The sale is allowed if he tells her when she returns
options.D: The sale is allowed because sales need less approval than purchases

questions.rationale: In an advisory account, the client makes each decision. Discretionary trading is prohibited outside discretionary and managed accounts under IDPC 3221. A trade without permission breaches the standards of conduct, even with good intent.
questions.source_quote: "Made trades in your account without your permission or used your funds in ways that you were unaware of" — research/sources/ciro/brochure-ciro-complaints-brochure.txt CIRO Complaints Brochure p.3, ~L60
